failure_summary.description: Search or filter results were left bare, not assigned and saved, or used a nested cache retrieval.
Agents added unrelated cache reads, domains, imports, sorting, calculations, or output code instead of limiting work to pending requests.
Agents failed to apply a new same-domain constraint to a suitable cached result or omitted a stated constraint.
A state abbreviation was put in city, or a combined neighborhood-and-city phrase was truncated.
An explicitly requested first-class preference was not passed to the flight search.

patch.reasoning: The skill already states the correct cache, location, and scope rules, so those are not repeated. A compact call-shape reminder makes the required assign/retrieve/filter/save sequence more concrete and reinforces limiting code to pending work. Explicit cabin-class field mapping addresses the uncovered flight-class omission.

edits.content: **Call shape and scope audit:** For each necessary result-producing call, assign its result and save that unchanged object under a fresh relevant key. For a cache update, use separate statements to retrieve the exact cached base into a variable, filter that base, assign the filtered result, and save it; never nest retrieval. Emit only operations for currently pending requested deliverables—no unrelated cache reads, duplicate work, imports, print/report loops, or speculative date calculations.

- **Map explicit flight cabin classes:** For a clearly stated economy-, business-, or first-class preference, use the corresponding lowercase `flight_class` value (`["economy"]`, `["business"]`, or `["first"]`) on the relevant flight search or same-domain filter. Do not omit an explicit class preference or map it to hotel `stars`.
